arxiv-2107-13121.title: Learning Site-Specific Probing Beams for Fast mmWave Beam Alignment
arxiv-2107-13121.creator: Yuqiang Heng, Jianhua Mo and Jeffrey G. Andrews
arxiv-2107-13121.description: Abstract Beam alignment – the process of finding an optimal directional beam pair – is a challenging procedure crucial to millimeter wave communication systems. We propose a novel beam alignment method that learns a site-specific probing codebook and uses the probing codebook measurements to predict the optimal narrow beam.

arxiv-2206-08736.title: Generalised Policy Improvement with Geometric Policy Composition
arxiv-2206-08736.creator: Shantanu Thakoor, Mark Rowland, Diana Borsa, Will Dabney, Rémi Munos, André Barreto
arxiv-2206-08736.description: Abstract We introduce a method for policy improvement that interpolates between the greedy approach of value-based reinforcement learning (RL) and the full planning approach typical of model-based RL. The new method builds on the concept of a geometric horizon model (GHM, also known as a γ \gamma -model), which models the discounted state-visitation distribution of a given policy.

arxiv-2208-13309.title: P-wave Sommerfeld enhancement near threshold: a simplified approach
arxiv-2208-13309.creator: Carlos H. de Lima, Alberto Tonero, Andres Vasquez, Rogerio Rosenfeld
arxiv-2208-13309.description: Abstract The calculation of P-wave Sommerfeld enhancement in processes with unstable particles in the final state is known to be divergent. In a complete description, where resonant (on-shell unstable particles) and non-resonant contributions are included, it has been shown that results are finite. For most beyond the Standard Model applications, these complete calculations are not readily available.

arxiv-2209-11100.title: Canadian Traveller Problem with Predictions
arxiv-2209-11100.creator: Evripidis Bampis, Bruno Escoffier, Michalis Xefteris
arxiv-2209-11100.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Evripidis Bampis, Bruno Escoffier, Michalis Xefteris. In this work, we consider the k k -Canadian Traveller Problem ( k k -CTP) under the learning-augmented framework proposed by Lykouris & Vassilvitskii [ 23 ] .

arxiv-2301-06718.title: Sparse and Integrative Principal Component Analysis for Multiview Data
arxiv-2301-06718.creator: Lin Xiao, Luo Xiao
arxiv-2301-06718.description: Abstract We consider dimension reduction of multiview data, which are emerging in scientific studies. Formulating multiview data as multivariate data with block structures corresponding to the different views, or views of data, we estimate top eigenvectors from multiview data that have two-fold sparsity, elementwise sparsity and blockwise sparsity.

arxiv-2405-07000.title: Multidegrees, families, and integral dependence
arxiv-2405-07000.creator: Yairon Cid-Ruiz, Claudia Polini, Bernd Ulrich
arxiv-2405-07000.description: Abstract . We study the behavior of multidegrees in families and the existence of numerical criteria to detect integral dependence. We show that mixed multiplicities of modules are upper semicontinuous functions when taking fibers and that projective degrees of rational maps are lower semicontinuous under specialization.

arxiv-2504-09833.title: PPF: Pre-training and Preservative Fine-tuning of Humanoid Locomotion via Model-Assumption-based Regularization
arxiv-2504-09833.creator: Hyunyoung Jung, Zhaoyuan Gu, Ye Zhao, Hae-Won Park, Sehoon Ha
arxiv-2504-09833.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hyunyoung Jung, Zhaoyuan Gu, Ye Zhao, Hae-Won Park, Sehoon Ha. Humanoid locomotion is a challenging task due to its inherent complexity and high-dimensional dynamics, as well as the need to adapt to diverse and unpredictable environments. In this work, we introduce a novel learning framework for effectively training a humanoid locomotion policy that imitates the behavior of a model-based controller while extending its capabilities to handle more complex locomotion tasks, such as more challenging terrain and higher velocity commands.

arxiv-2507-19822.title: Debunking Optimization Myths in Federated Learning for Medical Image Classification
arxiv-2507-19822.creator: Youngjoon Lee *, Hyukjoon Lee, Jinu Gong, Yang Cao, Joonhyuk Kang †
arxiv-2507-19822.description: Abstract Federated Learning (FL) is a collaborative learning method that enables decentralized model training while preserving data privacy. Despite its promise in medical imaging, recent FL methods are often sensitive to local factors such as optimizers and learning rates, limiting their robustness in practical deployments.

arxiv-2507-20480.title: Automated 3D-GS Registration and Fusion via Skeleton Alignment and Gaussian-Adaptive Features
arxiv-2507-20480.creator: Shiyang Liu, Dianyi Yang, Yu Gao, Bohan Ren, Yi Yang*, Mengyin Fu
arxiv-2507-20480.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Shiyang Liu, Dianyi Yang, Yu Gao, Bohan Ren, Yi Yang*, Mengyin Fu. In recent years, 3D Gaussian Splatting (3D-GS)-based scene representation demonstrates significant potential in real-time rendering and training efficiency. However, most existing methods primarily focus on single-map reconstruction, while the registration and fusion of multiple 3D-GS sub-maps remain underexplored. Existing methods typically rely on manual intervention to select a reference sub-map as a template and use point cloud matching for registration. Moreover, hard-threshold filtering of 3D-GS primitives often degrades rendering quality after fusion.

pmc-10627070.title: Study on the Relationship Between PTPRO Methylation in Plasma and Efficacy Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy in Patients with Early Breast Cancer
pmc-10627070.creator: Xiang-Wei Liu, Mei-Juan Hong, Yan-Yu Qu
pmc-10627070.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to explore the correlation between PTPRO methylation in plasma and the efficacy of neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) for early breast cancer (BC).MethodsEighty-two patients with early BC undergoing NAC were included. PTPRO methylation status in plasma before and after NAC was detected using methylation-specific PCR and the relationship between PTPRO methylation and NAC efficacy was analyzed.

pmc-12476285.title: The Calcium Conundrum: Hypercalcemia of Unknown Etiology
pmc-12476285.creator: Alp S Kahveci, Lindsay Moy, Mohamed M Eletrebi, Brittany Bettendorf
pmc-12476285.description: Hypercalcemia is a common clinical finding with a wide variety of clinical presentations and etiologies. The differential is broad and includes hyperparathyroidism, malignancy, medication adverse effects, endocrinopathies, and a variety of granulomatous diseases. We present the case of an 84-year-old woman with severe parathyroid hormone-independent hypercalcemia and elevated 1,25-OH Vitamin D. Non-necrotizing granulomas were identified on bone marrow biopsy.

pmc-12506212.title: Multimorbidity in India: an analysis of prevalence and patterns of chronicity of diseases among older adults using Study on global AGEing and adult health (SAGE) Wave 2
pmc-12506212.creator: Ananya Anurakta Pattanaik, Rikat ul ain Hashmi, Rutuparna Sibani Dandsena, Smiteerekha Sahoo, Priyanka Verma, Shishirendu Ghosal, Sushmita Kerketta, Srikanta Kanungo, Sanghamitra Pati
pmc-12506212.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundMultimorbidity, the coexistence of two or more chronic non-communicable diseases, poses a significant health challenge in India, particularly among older adults. Factors such as population ageing, lifestyle changes and urbanisation have led to an increasing burden of chronic diseases.MethodsData from the Study on Global Ageing and Adult Health Wave 2, which surveyed 11 818 individuals in India, were utilised, focusing on those aged 50 and above. The analysis included 7118 participants after excluding those with missing or incorrect data.

pmc-13242111.title: Updating the critical steps of the quality implementation framework: an umbrella review of reviews
pmc-13242111.creator: Kathrine Hald, Anne Gulbech Ording, Martin Jorsal, Julie Midtgaard, Louise A Ellis, Samantha Spanos, Lisa Pagano, Georgia Fisher, Abraham Wandersman, Jeffrey Braithwaite, Søren Paaske Johnsen
pmc-13242111.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThe Quality Implementation Framework (QIF) is a widely used process model in implementation science (IS). Since its publication in 2012, the field of IS has expanded considerably, yet QIF has never undergone formal revision. Given recent advances and the complexity in implementation research and practice, this study examines whether QIF continues to capture the full scope of implementation quality and its challenges.MethodsAn umbrella review of reviews was conducted on literature published between 2012 and 2025.

(a) Civil action by employees (1) Liability Any employer who violates section 2615 of this title shall be liable to any eligible employee affected— (A) for damages equal to— (i) the amount of— (I) any wages, salary, employment benefits.

uslaw-usc-t42-s14952.title: 42 U.S.C. § 14952 — Special rules for certain cases
uslaw-usc-t42-s14952.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s14952.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 143 (Intercountry Adoptions); Subchapter V (General Provisions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Authority to establish alternative procedures for adoption of children by relatives To the extent consistent with the Convention, the Secretary may establish by regulation alternative procedures for the adoption of children by individuals related to them by blood.
